raised.claim: The body exclusion only recognizes `.test.ts` and two hard-coded test roots, so other reviewable test naming conventions such as source-adjacent `.spec.ts` remain embedded.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a reviewable test is named `src/parser.spec.ts`, it matches `src/**/*.ts` but none of these exclusions; a large changed spec body therefore still consumes the context budget and can demote source files to diff-only, preserving the regression this change is intended to prevent.

raised.claim: The source guard checks textual regexes rather than the reader values, so both of its critical invariants can be bypassed while the test remains green.
raised.why_it_breaks: A call using raw `readFile` can include a comment containing `readFile: contextReader(` and satisfy the first regex, while `const filtered = contextReader(readFile); ... fileContent: filtered` evades the second regex; in the latter state test-file findings are silently dropped by gate or verification despite this guard passing.

raised.claim: The replay argument parser silently ignores positionals after the optional base SHA instead of rejecting a malformed command.
raised.why_it_breaks: For `ai-review-replay -- 418 wrong-base intended-base`, `intended-base` is discarded and the replay runs against `wrong-base`; because replay results drive model decisions, a typo can produce measurements for the wrong diff without any warning.

raised.claim: Overriding the code head does not provide historical PR metadata, so a historical replay can still use the PR's current title and body rather than the prompt metadata seen by the original review.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the PR body is edited after the selected historical head—for example to describe fixes or alter requirements—`--head <old-sha>` reads files from the old commit but sends the current description to the finder, making the advertised recall replay materially different from the original review.

raised.claim: The historical-head fallback assumes an arbitrary force-pushed-away commit can always be fetched directly by object ID, which Git servers may reject once the commit is unreachable from advertised refs.
raised.why_it_breaks: When `--head` names a commit removed by a force-push and the remote no longer advertises any ref reaching it, `git fetch origin <sha>` can fail with `not our ref`; the replay then aborts even though this unreachable-history case is the stated purpose of the new option.
